authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode exists. source.py builds a BasicHttpAuthenticator(config['email'], config['api_token']) unconditionally, and __main__.py constructs the Estuary shim with oauth2=None, so no OAuth path is registered at all. The user self-serves a token from id.atlassian.com and pastes it plus their account email and Jira host; there is no app registration and no refresh token. That is T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: Termination is a runtime disjunction inside ONE shared next_page_token(): if the body is a dict with startAt, prefer isLast, else compare startAt >= total, else (dict with startAt but neither field) return a token forever; if the body is a bare list, stop when the page is shorter than page_size. The schema forces a single static enum per stream, which cannot express either the fallback chain or the non-terminating third branch.

proposedShape.nonTerminatingWhen: dict envelope carries startAt but neither isLast nor total

unionMisfits.description: The offset does NOT advance by page size and does NOT advance by records received. For envelope responses it advances by the SERVER-ECHOED response_json['maxResults'], which Jira may cap below the requested value; for bare-list responses it advances by the CLIENT-side page_size constant, which silently skips records if Jira caps the page lower than 50. The Paginator union has no place to record which quantity the offset advances by.

The incremental bound is not a query parameter carrying a timestamp; it is a fragment of a JQL query string ("updated >= '2024/01/31 09:05'", Jira's slash-separated local-time format) concatenated with an optional project filter and an ORDER BY clause into the `jql` param. The declared formats (iso8601/unix_seconds/date) cannot describe it.

These two send no server-side bound at all. They iterate the parent issues stream incrementally and fetch every child page in full, then drop records whose cursor is below the start point in Python. So the binding is 'incremental' in state/emission terms but 'snapshot per parent' in request terms. The PullSpec union has no way to say the filtering is client-side.

Roughly half of the streams are child streams that re-run a parent stream in full for every sync, and some chain three deep (screens -> screen_tabs -> screen_tab_fields; issues -> issue_property_keys -> issue_properties). pathPlaceholders records WHAT fills the slot but not that the parent is a separate, separately-billed full sweep whose cost dominates. There is also no way to record that Issues is instantiated three times over (once per child stream) rather than shared.

Every stream carries a per-stream list of HTTP status codes that cause a slice to be logged and silently dropped rather than failed (400 everywhere by default; 401/403/404 added on ~8 streams). This is a data-completeness property with no home in the schema: a customer missing project permissions gets a clean sync with missing rows.

One host serves three independently versioned API families (/rest/api/3/, /rest/agile/1.0/, /rest/dev-status/1.0/) selected per stream by a class attribute. A single baseUrl plus a single apiVersionPinning string cannot represent a per-stream base path.

This connector is an Airbyte-CDK v0.52 source wrapped by estuary_cdk.shim_airbyte_cdk.CaptureShim, not a native Estuary connector. Consequences the schema cannot express: the stream list is code-static but is still delivered through an Airbyte discover() call; state is Airbyte per-stream STREAM state stored under bindingStateV1; a checkpoint is emitted on every Airbyte state message; and the process performs exactly one sweep then exits, so all cadence lives in the Flow spec above the connector.

abstained.streams[*].pull.*.paginator.terminateOn: next_page_token() picks the termination rule at RUNTIME from the response body: it prefers the envelope flag `isLast`, falls back to `total`, and for bare-list responses falls back to a short page. Only issues/projects/users are pinned by unit-test fixtures; for the remaining streams the recorded value is the branch most likely taken and is marked low/medium confidence. The mechanism itself (startAt/maxResults offset) is certain for every stream.
abstained.streams[*].schedules: No per-binding schedule exists. The shim runs one Airbyte read() sweep and exits; cadence is imposed by the Flow runtime, not by anything in this connector.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.incrementalP: The incremental lower bound is not a standalone query parameter: it is spliced into a JQL expression ("updated >= 'YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM'") sent as the `jql` param, in Jira's own slash-separated local-time format. issue_comments/issue_worklogs send no bound at all and filter client-side. See unionMisfits.
abstained.streams[18].primaryKey: issue_properties is keyed on /key (the property key) alone in the discovered catalog even though records from different issues share property keys; issueId is added by transform but is not part of the key. Recorded as the source states it, not as it should be.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Nothing in the connector or in its resourceConfigSchema carries an interval or cron. The shim performs a single read() sweep and exits; the cadence is set by the Flow capture spec outside this repository directory.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is poll over a stateless REST API. No server-side artifact is created, nothing accrues on the customer's side while we are stopped, and the only state is a client-held `updated` timestamp, so there is nothing for this field to describe.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static: source.py returns a hard-coded list of 55 stream classes (56 with the experimental one). The Airbyte discover() call that the shim makes only re-emits that fixed list, so there is no customer-schema discovery to describe.
abstained.streams[55].primaryKey: pull_requests is absent from the discover snapshot (enable_experimental_streams defaults to false); the key ['id'] is taken from schemas/pull_requests.json `required`, not from an observed catalog.
